base_member_text: [L1-L18,L21-L38] (MED/ignored-argument) Scalar text get/put accepts map but never uses it or rejects it, silently performing an unmapped strided transfer.
audit_member_text: [L1-L18,L21-L38] (MED/ignored-argument) The scalar text put/get interfaces accept map but never use it, silently performing strided rather than mapped transfers.

adversarial.rationale: Both complete scalar character procedures accept map but call only nf_*_vars_text and never reference map (netcdf_text_variables.f90:1-39). A scalar Fortran string still represents a character dimension, as netcdf.f90:30-34 explains, so scalar rank does not make a nonunit character-memory mapping meaningless.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L44-L45,L66-L69,L268-L269,L290-L293] (MED/contiguity-contract) Array text wrappers pass only the first scalar element of an assumed-shape array to bulk I/O, without packing or requiring contiguous actual arrays.
audit_member_text: [L66-L69,L98-L101,L290-L293,L482-L485] (MED/contiguity-contract) Assumed-shape character arrays are passed to the legacy routines by their first scalar element without packing or requiring contiguity, so noncontiguous array sections can access the wrong storage.

adversarial.rationale: The character dummy arrays are assumed-shape and have no CONTIGUOUS requirement, but each backend argument is a single first element (netcdf_text_variables.f90:42-71,266-295 and the higher-rank equivalents). The legacy routines are only EXTERNAL declarations in netcdf_externals.f90:32-46, so they receive neither the array descriptor nor its section strides; packing the scalar element cannot pack the remaining noncontiguous array.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L31-L38,L60-L69,L284-L293] (MED/buffer-extent-contract) Explicit count and map selections are forwarded without checking whether the requested character footprint fits the supplied string or array.
audit_member_text: [L15-L18,L35-L38,L285-L293] (MED/buffer-capacity) Explicit counts and maps are forwarded without checking their addressed span against the character buffer, allowing oversized otherwise-valid file selections to exceed values storage.

adversarial.rationale: Explicit count/map selections can exceed character storage and no wrapper checks their memory footprint, but oversized selections are a caller memory-contract violation; classify that generic omission as LOW defensive validation. The scalar put case involving an otherwise adequately sized string that is shortened by trim is a separate, stronger finding, and scalar map arguments are ignored rather than forwarded.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L56,L88,L248,L280,L472] (MED/default-count-inconsistency) Array text wrappers default trailing file-dimension counts to zero instead of one, so selecting a record of a higher-rank variable using start alone can transfer no data.
audit_member_text: [L56,L88,L120,L152,L184,L216,L248,L280,L312,L344,L376,L408,L440,L472] (MED/default-count) Trailing file dimensions default to zero counts, so writing or reading an array slice of a higher-rank variable can silently transfer no data unless every extra count is supplied.

adversarial.rationale: All fourteen array-text wrappers set counts above numDims+1 to zero, and a start-only call does not change them; scalar text and numeric wrappers instead use one. Thus an extra record dimension makes the selection empty even when the character-length and array dimensions are correctly sized; the backend zero-count behavior is documented in the [Unidata interface guide](https://docs.unidata.ucar.edu/netcdf-fortran/current/nc_f77_interface_guide.html).
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L55-L66,L279-L290,L471-L482] (MED/uninitialized-map) Array text wrappers initialize only numDims map entries although character storage needs numDims+1, leaving the last active stride undefined when the supplied map is shorter.
audit_member_text: [L55-L66,L279-L290,L471-L482] (HIGH/uninitialized-map) Array text wrappers initialize only numDims map entries despite transferring numDims+1 character dimensions, so a partial map leaves an active mapping entry uninitialized.

adversarial.rationale: Retain at MED for mapped calls whose supplied map omits an active character-array dimension, particularly when that dimension has more than one selected element. Unmapped calls bypass localMap entirely and a full map replaces the missing entry, so the HIGH wording should not imply a general array-text failure.

     else
       nf90_put_var_1D_text = &
          nf_put_vars_text(ncid, varid, localStart, localCount, localStride, values(1))
     end if

base_member_text: [L11-L18] (MED/buffer-extent) Scalar text put always passes trim(values), so an explicit count including trailing blanks can request more characters than the temporary contains.
audit_member_text: [L11,L15,L18] (MED/buffer-contract) Scalar text writes always pass trim(values), even when an explicit count requests trailing characters that were removed from the actual buffer.

adversarial.rationale: An explicit count overwrites len_trim(values), but the backend actual remains trim(values) unconditionally (netcdf_text_variables.f90:9-18). For example a length-two value ending in a blank with count=(/2/) supplies only a length-one temporary; neither the default-count assignment nor another module restores the removed blank.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L66-L69,L290-L293,L482-L485] (LOW/empty-array) Array text wrappers form the first-element actual argument even for empty arrays, before a zero transfer count can neutralize the lower-level operation.
audit_member_text: [L66-L69,L290-L293] (LOW/empty-array-contract) The wrappers form values(1) even for zero-length arrays, leaving empty transfers dependent on an out-of-bounds element reference before the backend can honor a zero count.

adversarial.rationale: Each array-text transfer forms values(1) or its higher-rank equivalent without testing size(values), in both mapped and unmapped branches (netcdf_text_variables.f90:63-70,287-294). A zero selection can prevent backend I/O but cannot make that first-element argument designate an existing element of an empty array; this is correctly limited to a LOW language/bounds-contract issue.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L7-L16,L50-L64,L466-L480] (MED/array-bounds) Optional indexing vectors are copied into fixed-size arrays without validating their lengths.
audit_member_text: [L14-L16,L60-L64,L284-L288,L476-L480] (MED/bounds) Optional index vectors are copied into fixed-size local arrays without checking their lengths against nf90_max_var_dims.

adversarial.rationale: The fixed-vector copies are unchecked, but the overrun requires caller vectors longer than nf90_max_var_dims=1024, not a valid file rank. Retain as LOW input-contract validation; scalar map is ignored and therefore is not itself copied into a fixed local array.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L186,L218,L410,L442,L474] (LOW/integer-overflow) Default character map strides use default-INTEGER products that can overflow for large string arrays.
